messages:
ashley.k: Heads up — incident in eu-controlplane just tripped a canary (503s) during the 03:00 window. I'm pausing the next two release slots until we confirm root cause.

deploy-bot: Release slot 8745 PAUSED by ashley.k — reason: incident/eu-controlplane 503 spike. Canary instances removed from rotation.

mario: Copy. What's the signal? latency or 5xx count?

ashley.k: Mostly 503s from the frontend LB to orbit-router, correlated with a KV cache flurry — saw large eviction churn in logs.

ops-oncall: I'm on it. Gathering controlplane logs now. Looks like a spike in connection resets around 02:58.

sre-olivia: Can we avoid a full rollback? Maybe swap the canary to the previous image on the same slot and re-run smoke tests. That keeps release timeline shorter.

jonah: Agreed, prefer canary-swap over global rollback if the old canary is healthy. We should pin the running version for affected slots to avoid flapping.

ashley.k: Plan: 1) Keep slots paused. 2) Swap canary in slot 8745 -> revert to image v2.3.7. 3) Run quick smoke + synthetic. 4) If green, requeue slot with sticky pin for 1h, otherwise escalate to rollback. Thoughts?

mario: Works for me. If smoke fails, we auto-run rollback playbook and notify customers. Can deploy-bot do the swap and pin?

deploy-bot: Executing canary swap: slot 8745 -> image v2.3.7 (requested by ashley.k). Applying sticky_pin="v2.3.7" for 3600s. Smoke tests queued.

ops-oncall: Smoke tests started — 12 tests, focusing on happy-path inference, auth, and ingress.

sre-olivia: Also enable extra tracing for KV cache ops in those slots for next 30m. Add a label so logs are easy to grep.

jonah: I'll draft a short blurb for release notes and a pinned thread for execs in case this becomes multi-slot. Keep it minimal: "hold due to eu controlplane 503s; canary swapped; monitoring."

deploy-bot: Smoke tests: 12/12 PASS for slot 8745. Canary swap succeeded. Sticky pin active.

ashley.k: Nice. Ops — continue log sampling for 15 more minutes then decide on requeue. If noise persists, we roll back the deploy window for EU and open an incident review.

ops-oncall: Sampling now. So far the 503 spike hasn't reappeared on the reverted canary.

sre-olivia: I'm seeing reduced eviction churn after the swap; looks correlated with the newer image's memory behavior. We'll keep tracing on.

mario: Can we requeue slot with throttled ramp? e.g., 10% at t+10, 25% at t+20 to watch for recurrence.

ashley.k: Yes — requeue with staged rollout and ops hold for immediate pause if the metric crosses thresholds. deploy-bot, schedule requeue with ramp policy.

deploy-bot: Requeue scheduled for slot 8745 in +15m with staged rollout [10% -> 25% -> 100%], auto-pause thresholds: 5xx_rate>1% OR latency_p50>500ms. Notifying release owners.

jonah: I'll update the release notes: "Incident-triggered hold in EU. Canary rolled back to v2.3.7, staged requeue scheduled. Investigating KV cache eviction root cause; follow-up postmortem to come"

ashley.k: Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If everything stays green by +45m we lift the hold for the rest of the window.

ops-oncall: +1 — will post final status at +45m or earlier if we need to reopen. :thumbsup:
